svg.title: Catalyst's Four Compilation Phases, Traced Through One Query
svg.desc: A worked example tracing a filtered join query through Catalyst's four sequential compilation phases — unresolved logical plan, analyzed logical plan, optimized logical plan, and physical plan — then into physical-plan selection and the RDD execution graph Spark actually runs.
svg.text: Catalyst's Four Compilation Phases — Traced Through One Query
Unresolved logical plan ➔ Analyzed logical plan ➔ Optimized logical plan ➔ Physical plan ➔ RDD execution

g.text: SELECT o.order_id, c.name FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.cust_id = c.cust_id WHERE o.amount > 100

g.aria-label: Phase 1: Unresolved logical plan — parser output with names still unchecked strings
Phase 2: Analyzed logical plan — catalog resolution binds names to typed schema objects
g.text: Catalog binds every name to a

g.aria-label: Phase 3: Optimized logical plan — rule-based rewrites push predicates and prune columns
Phase 4: Selected physical plan — concrete algorithms chosen and costed
Physical plan candidates and cost model — multiple physical strategies generated and costed before one is selected
g.text: One logical Join maps to more than one physical candidate — the cost model picks the winner:
cutoff for broadcasting one join side

svg.text: Lowest-cost candidate selected → feeds Phase 4 above

g.aria-label: SQL or DataFrame query text — the starting point before compilation begins
g.text: Both forms parse into the identical

g.aria-label: RDD execution graph — runtime stages, tasks, and Adaptive Query Execution re-planning after compilation ends
g.text: RDD execution graph (runtime) — compilation ends here; execution begins
Physical plan compiles into stages/tasks scheduled across executors. Adaptive Query Execution (default on
since Spark 3.2.0) can re-plan remaining stages using stats from completed stages — e.g. converting a
planned SortMergeJoin to BroadcastHashJoin at runtime if actual sizes differ from the phase-4 estimate.
HOW TO OBSERVE EACH PHASE DIRECTLY
prints all four plans in order — parsed (unresolved), analyzed, optimized, and physical.
Default df.explain() prints the physical plan alone; "formatted" adds per-node detail blocks; "cost" annotates the logical plan with statistics; "codegen" shows the fused generated code.
⚠ TWO REAL FAILURE POINTS ALONG THIS PIPELINE
any optimization or execution planning runs. The
cost of catching it here is cheap by comparison.
Evidence: EXPLAIN EXTENDED / Apache Spark docs
Wrapping a filtered column in a function or cast
pushdown. PushedFilters: [] appears in the Phase 4
physical plan — invisible unless that plan is read.
Evidence: Spark SQL Performance Tuning docs

svg.text: Scope note: this diagram stays inside the four sequential compilation phases with a worked trace; whole-stage code generation and the Native Execution Engine branch are covered separately in spark-catalyst-query-compilation.
Source: Apache Spark SQL documentation (EXPLAIN reference, Performance Tuning guide) — tier 3. Fabric Codex original composition.
